svg.text: Personal workspace edition. Every arrow is a real call path in the code. Magenta marks the rules that gate an assistant: nothing answers or works without an approved, validly signed release.
Workspace · Assistants · Workflows · Model Studio · Evaluations · Approvals · Activity (+ legacy Advanced pages)
Pure functions of one snapshot; the chain Recipe → Dataset → Candidate → Evaluation → Release → Assistant is the navigation.
browser.ts · home-view.ts · studio-view.ts · workflow-view.ts · review-views.ts · flow-model.ts · units.ts · ui.ts
Analyze / Build / Review against a Git repo. Worker: local model or an approved
assistant, with its learning schedule and Learn now. Diffs are reviewed before apply.
Any MCP client with the workspace's bearer token:
scripts, other workspaces, the extension itself.
HTTP SERVER · workbench/server.ts (session cookie for the browser, bearer only at the two MCP endpoints)
ENGINES · each one owns its records and its rules; a page never decides state on its own
project → dataset (validated; secrets counted, never shown) → config + training job
→ candidate artifact → evaluation (readiness suite vs recipe or last release)
→ release (content hash; distinct reviewers sign) → assistant (own instructions)
Recipes are code: coding, IT support, incident, knowledge, Jira, Salesforce delivery.
Evidence is re-derived, never trusted: data and scores are recomputed before use.
resolveProfile(): active profile + approved, validly signed release, or refuse
studio/engine.ts · schema.ts · recipes.ts · dataset.ts · evaluation.ts · store.ts
One answer to "can this assistant work
Persona from the release; tools only from
the workspace MCP. Ollama via chat-config.
Definition: stages with agent, instructions, review gate,
Jira status, bot policy, optional assistant (agentic unit).
Runs freeze their config; outputs hashed; gates need
distinct reviewers; owner and author cannot self approve.
Templates as code: development, Salesforce delivery.
guard: bind and start refuse an unusable assistant
tick: one job per run and stage staffed by an assistant; run
with a fresh binding; attach a draft. Never completes or approves.
per project: manual, daily or weekly, with an import folder pattern.
Cycle: import → validate → train → evaluate → release; people gate it.
learning-schedule.ts → studio commands as the owner
Registry, approvals and audit (approved agent definitions)
Draft → submitted → approved: distinct reviewer signatures over a definition hash;
workflow policy (roles, required approvals); audit trail. Feeds the workspace MCP.
Bot runtime and editor session (code work on a repository)
Git checkout per run; the model reads files through allowed tools and proposes file changes;
a person reviews and applies them. A stage bound to an assistant runs with its model and instructions.
Every stage transition becomes a Jira preview
(create or update issue). Delivery is a local admin action.
Training provider: local-dev today (deterministic placeholder artifact, "no weights were trained"); the interface is where Azure or another real provider plugs in.
Evaluator: development readiness metrics (record validity, uniqueness, secret hygiene, coverage). Chat and drafting models: local Ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434, the release's base model.
STORAGE · local application data directory, one JSON document per workspace, atomic rename is the commit point
